q: Materials which have an electrical resistance that lies between the high resistance values of insulators and the low resistance values of metals are called ____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. Materials which have an electrical resistance that lies between the high resistance values of insulators and the low resistance values of metals are called semiconductors.

q: For example, ____ and silicon are commonly used semiconductors.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. For example, germanium and silicon are commonly used semiconductors.

q: Gallium arsenide(GaAs) and ____ are used as semiconductors.
e: Ge and Si are elemental semiconductors. GaAs and CdTe are compound semiconductors. Gallium arsenide(GaAs) and Cadmium Telluride(CdTe) are used as semiconductors.

q: They are ____ semiconductors.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. They are compound semiconductors.

q: In metals, ____ are the charge carriers.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. In metals, electrons are the charge carriers.

q: In the case of semiconductors, both electrons and ____ are the charge carriers.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. In the case of semiconductors, both electrons and positive holes are the charge carriers.

q: A vacancy which is left by an electron in the semiconductor atom is called a ____.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. A vacancy which is left by an electron in the semiconductor atom is called a positive hole.

q: When the potential is applied to two ends of a semiconductor, electrons moves from lower potential to higher one, while the ____ move in the opposite direction.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. When the potential is applied to two ends of a semiconductor, electrons moves from lower potential to higher one, while the positive holes move in the opposite direction.

q: This means that the current flows due to the movement of ____ in the case of semiconductors.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. This means that the current flows due to the movement of electrons and holes in the case of semiconductors.

q: Pure semiconductors have ____ of electrons, and positive holes.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. Pure semiconductors have equal numbers of electrons, and positive holes.

q: Since these are relatively few in number at normal temperature, pure semiconductors have ____.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. Since these are relatively few in number at normal temperature, pure semiconductors have poor conductivity.

q: When a few ____ are added to the pure semiconductor, its conductivity increases.
e: A little donor or acceptor impurity, doping, makes n-type or p-type material and raises conductivity. When a few impurity atoms are added to the pure semiconductor, its conductivity increases.

q: Arsenic, aluminium and ____ atoms are used as impurity atoms.
e: A little donor or acceptor impurity, doping, makes n-type or p-type material and raises conductivity. Arsenic, aluminium and indium atoms are used as impurity atoms.

q: As a result, ____ types of semiconductor are obtained.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. As a result, two types of semiconductor are obtained.

q: When arsenic atoms having ____ valence electrons are added to the pure semiconductor (Ge, Si) atoms having four valence electrons, the conductivity of pure semiconductor increases.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. When arsenic atoms having five valence electrons are added to the pure semiconductor (Ge, Si) atoms having four valence electrons, the conductivity of pure semiconductor increases.

q: Since the number of electrons is greater than that of positive holes in this impure semiconductor it is called an ____.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. Since the number of electrons is greater than that of positive holes in this impure semiconductor it is called an n-type semiconductor.

q: In the n-type semiconductor ____ are the majority charge carriers of electric current.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. In the n-type semiconductor electrons are the majority charge carriers of electric current.

q: When indium atoms having ____ valence electrons are added to pure semiconductor(Ge, Si) atoms having four valence electrons, the conductivity of pure semiconductor increases.
e: A group-V atom (five valence electrons) donates an electron. A group-III atom (three valence electrons) accepts one and leaves a hole. When indium atoms having three valence electrons are added to pure semiconductor(Ge, Si) atoms having four valence electrons, the conductivity of pure semiconductor increases.

q: Since the number of positive holes is greater than that of electrons in this impure semiconductor it is called a ____.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. Since the number of positive holes is greater than that of electrons in this impure semiconductor it is called a p-type semiconductor.

q: Thus in a p-type semiconductor ____ are the majority charge carriers of electric current.
e: A group-III acceptor makes a p-type semiconductor. Holes are the majority carriers. Thus in a p-type semiconductor positive holes are the majority charge carriers of electric current.

q: A boundary or junction is formed between p-type and n-type semiconductors by semiconductor device fabrication process, and this junction is called a ____.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. A boundary or junction is formed between p-type and n-type semiconductors by semiconductor device fabrication process, and this junction is called a p-n junction.

q: A device which consists of a p-n junction is called a ____.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. A device which consists of a p-n junction is called a p-n junction diode.

q: When a battery is joined with its negative terminal to the p-type and its positive terminal to the n-type, only a very small current flows through the p-n junction diode, and it is said to be ____.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. When a battery is joined with its negative terminal to the p-type and its positive terminal to the n-type, only a very small current flows through the p-n junction diode, and it is said to be reverse-biased.

q: It means that the current flows in ____ only from the anode to the cathode in a vacuum diode and from p to n in a p-n junction diode.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. It means that the current flows in one direction only from the anode to the cathode in a vacuum diode and from p to n in a p-n junction diode.

q: Anode and cathode of a p-n junction, not in connection with a battery, are not at the same electric potential because there is initially a ____ across the junction.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. Anode and cathode of a p-n junction, not in connection with a battery, are not at the same electric potential because there is initially a potential difference across the junction.

q: A rectifier is a device which converts an alternating current (AC) into a unidirectional current or a ____.
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. A rectifier is a device which converts an alternating current (AC) into a unidirectional current or a direct current (DC).

q: Diodes can be used as rectifiers because the current flows in ____ only from anode to cathode.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. Diodes can be used as rectifiers because the current flows in one direction only from anode to cathode.

q: The diagram shown in Figure 11.5 (a) is that of a ____.
e: The diagram shown in Figure 11.5 (a) is that of a half-wave rectifier. Half-wave rectifier is what this statement is using.

q: There is only ____ diode in the half-wave rectifier circuit.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. There is only one diode in the half-wave rectifier circuit.

q: As the current I flows in the diode for every first half of the cycle of AC, this device acts as a ____.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. As the current I flows in the diode for every first half of the cycle of AC, this device acts as a half-wave rectifier.

q: The circuit diagram shown in Figure 11.6(a) is that of a ____.
e: The circuit diagram shown in Figure 11.6(a) is that of a full-wave rectifier. Full-wave rectifier is what this statement is using.

q: The full-wave rectifier circuit consists of ____ diodes.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. The full-wave rectifier circuit consists of two diodes.

q: Since D1 and D2 operate ____ for one cycle of an AC voltage, current always flows through the resistor R.
e: Since D1 and D2 operate alternately for one cycle of an AC voltage, current always flows through the resistor R. Alternately is what this statement is using. Alternately is what this sentence is naming.

q: As the current flows through R for both half-cycle of the AC voltage, this device is called a ____.
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. As the current flows through R for both half-cycle of the AC voltage, this device is called a full-wave rectifier.

q: The principal application of a rectifier is to convert ____.
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. The principal application of a rectifier is to convert AC to DC.

q: Most of the electronic devices require ____ for their operation.
e: Most of the electronic devices require DC power for their operation. Dc power is what this statement is using.
